extraction.name: VideoChat-Flash
extraction.description: A video Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) designed for long-context video understanding, featuring hierarchical video token compression (HiCo) to efficiently process long videos while preserving essential details. It introduces a large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset (LongVid) and a challenging 'Multi-Hop Needle-In-A-Video-Haystack' benchmark for evaluation.
extraction.creator: Shanghai AI Laboratory, Nanjing University, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai Innovation Institute
extraction.citeAs: VideoChat-Flash: Hierarchical Compression for Long-Context Video Modeling
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset LongVid was constructed by leveraging existing high-quality video datasets (Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, MiraData) and generating dense event labels for each long video. Captions from these datasets were used to create sequences of event labels with timestamps, and QA pairs were generated based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: LongVid was curated from Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData, which include movies, egocentric videos, news, interviews, how-to videos, and other in-the-wild videos of long duration.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Video data was segmented into clips, encoded using a video encoder with spatio-temporal attention, and compressed via token merging. A multi-stage short-to-long learning scheme was employed, involving video-language alignment, short video pre-training, joint short & long video instruction tuning, and high-resolution post-finetuning.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were segmented into clips, frames were sampled based on duration, and spatio-temporal compression was applied. Timestamp prompts were used to enable timestamp perception. Progressive visual dropout was applied during LLM inference to reduce redundancy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were generated by leveraging existing high-quality captions from source datasets (e.g., Panda-70M, CosMo, Ego4D-HCap, MiraData). For datasets without event-level annotations, major events were extracted using an LLM. QA pairs were constructed based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: LLM-based extraction and annotation (Qwen-72b) were used for event and background label extraction. Human-annotated captions and QA pairs from MS-COCO were used for benchmark evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process involved filtering and regrouping existing captions to form long video sequences and constructing QA pairs based on these captions and event labels. For the 'Multi-Hop Needle-In-A-Video-Haystack' benchmark, multiple reasoning paths were inserted to evaluate complex reasoning abilities.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3,444,849 QA pairs across five task types (video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, video event counting) for 114,228 long videos.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: LLM-based extraction (Qwen-72b), token merging for video compression, spatio-temporal attention in video encoding, and progressive visual dropout during LLM inference.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Potentially includes personal attributes such as age, gender, and socio-economic status in egocentric videos (e.g., Ego4D).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and model aim to advance long-context video understanding, which could have applications in surveillance, education, and entertainment. However, biases in training data (e.g., overrepresentation of certain activities or demographics) may lead to skewed model performance.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Biases may arise from the overrepresentation of certain video types (e.g., how-to videos, egocentric videos) and the use of automated captioning tools, which could introduce inconsistencies or inaccuracies in annotations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may not generalize well to videos outside the domains represented in the source datasets (e.g., movies, egocentric videos, news). The automated annotation process may introduce noise or inaccuracies in event labels and QA pairs.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and fine-tuning of video Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for long-context video understanding tasks, including video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting. The model is designed for applications requiring long video comprehension, such as surveillance, education, and entertainment.
